addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
Now I have a complete picture. Let me provide the comprehensive report.

---

Here is a thorough analysis of how derived metadata is computed from memo content in this codebase.

## 1. Where Memo Metadata Is Computed/Derived from Content

There are two distinct categories of derived metadata: **persisted payload** (stored in the database) and **on-the-fly computed fields** (generated at API response time).

### A. Persisted Payload (Tags + Property) -- via `RebuildMemoPayload`

The core function is `RebuildMemoPayload` in:

**`/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`** (lines 74-88)

This function calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` on `memo.Content` and stores two things into `memo.Payload`:
- `memo.Payload.Tags` -- list of `#tags` found in the content
- `memo.Payload.Property` -- a `MemoPayload_Property` struct

The `ExtractAll` method is defined in:

**`/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`** (lines 356-422)

It parses the markdown content into an AST and walks it once to extract:

1. **Tags** (`[]string`) -- all `#tag` nodes (excluding tags inside links/images), deduplicated while preserving case
2. **Mentions** (`[]string`) -- all `@mention` nodes, lowercased and deduplicated
3. **Property** (`*storepb.MemoPayload_Property`) containing:
   - **`Title`** (`string`) -- extracted from the first block-level child of the document IF it is an H1 heading (`# Heading`). Only the first block element is checked; if it is not an H1, title remains empty.
   - **`HasLink`** (`bool`) -- true if any `gast.KindLink` node is found
   - **`HasCode`** (`bool`) -- true if any code block, fenced code block, or code span is found
   - **`HasTaskList`** (`bool`) -- true if any GFM task checkbox is found
   - **`HasIncompleteTasks`** (`bool`) -- true if any unchecked task checkbox is found

The proto definition for the persisted payload is in:

**`/bench/home/work/proto/store/memo.proto`** (lines 7-29)

```protobuf
message MemoPayload {
  Property property = 1;
  Location location = 2;
  repeated string tags = 3;

  message Property {
    bool has_link = 1;
    bool has_task_list = 2;
    bool has_code = 3;
    bool has_incomplete_tasks = 4;
    string title = 5;
  }
}
```

### B. On-the-fly Computed Fields -- Snippet

The **snippet** is NOT persisted in the database. It is computed at API response time every time a memo is serialized.

**`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`** (lines 83-90) defines `getMemoContentSnippet`:

```go
func (s *APIV1Service) getMemoContentSnippet(content string) (string, error) {
	snippet, err := s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)
```

It calls `GenerateSnippet` in **`/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`** (lines 264-346) which:
- Parses the markdown into an AST
- Walks it, extracting plain text from all nodes (skipping code blocks, preserving inline code)
- Adds spaces between block-level elements (paragraphs, headings, list items, table cells)
- Truncates at a word boundary at 64 characters (the hard-coded max in `getMemoContentSnippet`)
- Appends " ..." if truncated

The snippet is attached to the API response in:

**`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`** (lines 76-81)

```go
snippet, err := s.getMemoContentSnippet(memo.Content)
...
memoMessage.Snippet = snippet
```

The API proto definition for the Memo message with the snippet field is in:

**`/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`** (lines 265-266)

```protobuf
// Output only. The snippet of the memo content. Plain text only.
string snippet = 17 [(google.api.field_behavior) = OUTPUT_ONLY];
```

### C. RSS Feed Title Generation

The RSS service computes its own title from memo content (separate from the payload title):

**`/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go`** (lines 302-336) `generateItemTitle`:
- Takes the first line of the content
- Strips markdown heading syntax (`#` through `######`)
- Truncates at 100 characters at a word boundary
- Falls back to "Memo" if empty

It also renders the full content to HTML for the RSS `description` and `content:encoded` fields at lines 338-344.

## 2. What Triggers Recomputation

### On CreateMemo (persisted payload computed)

**`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`** (line 108):
```go
if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService); err != nil {
```
Called during `CreateMemo` before the memo is persisted to the database. This also applies to comments since `CreateMemoComment` calls `CreateMemo` internally (see `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`, line 56).

### On UpdateMemo (persisted payload re-computed only when content changes)

**`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`** (lines 434-451):
The `UpdateMemo` handler iterates over `request.UpdateMask.Paths`. Only when the path `"content"` is in the update mask does it call `RebuildMemoPayload`:
```go
if path == "content" {
    ...
    if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService); err != nil {
```
Other update paths (visibility, pinned, state, timestamps, location, attachments, relations) do NOT trigger payload rebuild.

### Batch Rebuild (all memos)

**`/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`** (lines 27-72) `RunOnce`:
Iterates through ALL memos in batches of 100, calling `RebuildMemoPayload` on each and updating the database. This is available as a utility but is NOT currently called during server startup (the `startBackgroundRunners` in `server.go` only starts the S3 presign runner). It exists as infrastructure that can be invoked for migrations or manual repair.

### Snippet (on every read)

The snippet is computed on-the-fly during every API response serialization. It is triggered by:
- `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` -- called by every Get/List/Create/Update memo endpoint (line 76 of `memo_service_converter.go`)
- `batchConvertMemoRelations` -- when `includeSnippets=true`, generates snippets for related memos (lines 225-230, 248 of `memo_service_converter.go`)
- `convertMemoRelationFromStore` -- generates snippets for both sides of a relation (lines 154, 162 of `memo_relation_service.go`)
- `memoNotificationSnippet` -- for notification payloads (line 323 of `user_service_notifications.go`)

### Mention extraction (for notifications)

**`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`** (line 32) calls `ExtractAll` to parse @mentions from content for dispatching mention notifications. This is triggered on both create and update.

## 3. Summary of All Derived Properties

| Property | Persisted? | Source Field | How Extracted | Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tags` | Yes (in `Payload`) | `Content` | All `#tag` AST nodes (excluding inside links/images) | Create, Update(content) |
| `property.title` | Yes (in `Payload`) | `Content` | Plain text of the first block element if it's an H1 heading | Create, Update(content) |
| `property.has_link` | Yes (in `Payload`) | `Content` | Any `Link` AST node | Create, Update(content) |
| `property.has_code` | Yes (in `Payload`) | `Content` | Any code block, fenced code block, or code span | Create, Update(content) |
| `property.has_task_list` | Yes (in `Payload`) | `Content` | Any GFM `TaskCheckBox` node | Create, Update(content) |
| `property.has_incomplete_tasks` | Yes (in `Payload`) | `Content` | Any unchecked `TaskCheckBox` | Create, Update(content) |
| `snippet` | No (computed on read) | `Content` | Plain text extraction, code blocks stripped, 64-char truncation at word boundary | Every API response |
| `mentions` | Not stored on memo | `Content` | `@username` AST nodes, lowercased | Create, Update(content) -- used for inbox notifications |
| RSS `title` | Not stored | `Content` | First line, strip heading markup, truncate at 100 chars | RSS feed generation |
| RSS `description` | Not stored | `Content` | Full markdown rendered to HTML via goldmark | RSS feed generation |

### Key Files

- **`/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`** -- Core extraction engine (`ExtractAll`, `ExtractTags`, `ExtractProperties`, `GenerateSnippet`)
- **`/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`** -- `RebuildMemoPayload` function and batch runner
- **`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`** -- `CreateMemo` (line 108) and `UpdateMemo` (line 447) trigger recomputation
- **`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`** -- Converts store memo to API memo, attaches snippet (line 76) and property (line 49)
- **`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`** -- `getMemoContentSnippet` definition (line 83)
- **`/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`** -- Mention extraction from content (line 32)
- **`/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go`** -- RSS title and HTML description generation (lines 302-344)
- **`/bench/home/work/proto/store/memo.proto`** -- Persisted `MemoPayload` schema
- **`/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`** -- API `Memo` message with `snippet` (line 266), `tags` (line 241), `property` (line 256)
- **`/bench/home/work/store/memo.go`** -- Store-level `Memo` struct with `Payload *storepb.MemoPayload` (line 51)

h14.

The derived metadata is computed primarily in two places: **`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`** (`RebuildMemoPayload`) for persisted payload properties, and **`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`** / **`memo_service_webhooks.go`** for the on-the-fly snippet.

**Computation site:** `RebuildMemoPayload` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` calls `MarkdownService.ExtractAll()` (defined in `internal/markdown/markdown.go`) to parse the memo's markdown content into an AST and walk it to extract metadata. The snippet is computed separately via `GenerateSnippet()` in `internal/markdown/markdown.go`, invoked at API response time through `convertMemoFromStore` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`.

**Triggers for recomputation:**
- **CreateMemo** — `RebuildMemoPayload` is called before persisting (`memo_service.go`, ~line 108).
- **UpdateMemo** — `RebuildMemoPayload` is called only when `"content"` is in the `UpdateMask.Paths` (`memo_service.go`, ~line 447); other field updates (visibility, pinned, etc.) do not trigger it.
- **Every API read** — The `snippet` field is computed on-the-fly each time a memo is serialized for an API response.
- **Batch rebuild** — `RunOnce` in `memopayload/runner.go` iterates all memos in batches of 100 and rebuilds each payload (for migrations/repair).

**Extracted properties (persisted in `MemoPayload`):**
- **`property.title`** (`string`) — plain text of the first block element if it is an H1 heading; empty otherwise.
- **`property.has_link`** (`bool`) — whether any link node exists in the AST.
- **`property.has_code`** (`bool`) — whether any code block, fenced code block, or code span exists.
- **`property.has_task_list`** (`bool`) — whether any GFM task checkbox exists.
- **`property.has_incomplete_tasks`** (`bool`) — whether any unchecked task checkbox exists.
- **`tags`** (`[]string`) — all `#tag` nodes (excluding those inside links/images), deduplicated.

**Extracted on-the-fly:**
- **`snippet`** (`string`) — plain-text extraction from the markdown AST (code blocks stripped, inline code kept), truncated at 64 characters on a word boundary with `" ..."` appended if truncated. Marked `OUTPUT_ONLY` in the API proto (`proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto:265`).
